carmen-ml: Heads up — ran a PTQ pass on mt-rerank-v3 (INT8) and the dev MRR looks fine but NDCG@10 dropped ~6% compared to FP16. Not sure if it's a true quality regression or a formatting mismatch between eval and serving.
dmitri-rs: hmm, 6% is notable. Did you run the exact same candidate ordering and tie-breaking? PTQ can change tokenization boundaries slightly if the eval code uses a different tokenizer/state.
carmen-ml: ordering is the same (we seed shuffles). Eval command I used:
```bash
python eval/rerank_eval.py --model mt-rerank-v3 --weights ptq/int8/mt-rerank-v3.pt --dataset openset-dev --truncate right --max_len 1024 --batch 64 --seed 42
```
I attached a tiny diff of the top-5 reranked IDs for an example query — FP16 vs INT8 differ in rank for some long docs.
ben-infra: can you paste the token counts for the examples where ranks diverge? If INT8 ends up truncating 1-2 tokens earlier due to tokenization mismatch it could change document context for the reranker.
dmitri-rs: also check whether eval pipeline uses the same `tokenizer.pad_to_max_length` / `truncation_side`. We've seen `right` vs `left` default drift across repos cause subtle NDCG hits.
elena-pm: quick Q — which dataset is "openset-dev" vs the internal benchmark? we saw discrepancies before when dev had shorter queries.
carmen-ml: openset-dev is the public dev split; our holdout (internal-holdout-v2) is longer tail. The regressions are concentrated on queries with avg doc length > 900 tokens. Short queries (<200 tokens) are OK.
eval-bot: automated-run: mt-rerank-v3 INT8 smoke — NDCG@10: 0.742 (FP16 baseline 0.793), MRR@10: 0.521 (baseline 0.528). More details: /runs/1749991111
dmitri-rs: ok so it's a long-document edgecase. Two hypotheses: (1) PTQ quantization changed attention kernel numerics and harms long-seq interactions; (2) our evaluation truncation/prefix-preservation logic differs between the embedding/candidate prep step and the reranker runtime.
ben-infra: I can spin a small Dedicated job to run INT8 vs FP16 at variable `max_len` (512/1024/2048) and same tokenizer flags. Want me to run it? will take ~4h.
carmen-ml: please run it. Also add a run where we use `truncate=left` for docs (keep the end context) — anecdotal that relevance often lives near the end for long docs.
dmitri-rs: add one more ablation: force re-tokenize candidates with `use_fast=False` to rule out fast tokenizer differences.
elena-pm: from product POV — if this is a quantization-only regression on long docs, should we gate INT8 rollout for customers with long-doc workloads? happy to draft a small note once we have the ablation results.
carmen-ml: plan: (1) infra job for len sweep + tokenizer flags (ben), (2) seed sweep x3 to check variance (dmitri), (3) compare per-query top-k diffs and tokenization diffs (me). I'll post results in this thread.
eval-bot: job-1749991111 started on dedicated-us-west (approx eta 3.9h) :gear:
ben-infra: started. configs queued: [FP16/INT8] x [max_len=512,1024,2048] x [truncate=right,left] x [use_fast=True,False]. Will upload logs as they finish.
carmen-ml: thanks — if we see the regression only at 2048 with right truncation then action is to prefer left-truncate for INT8 rollout + add an eval guard.
dmitri-rs: also add a cheap synthetic test: a constructed doc where ground truth is in the last 128 tokens. If INT8 loses that signal, it's more likely a truncation/tokenization mismatch rather than pure numeric degradation.
carmen-ml: added the synthetic test to the job. will follow up with a short summary and example diffs once jobs complete. :thumbsup:
